one_variable_vs_v4: corpus quality (dense-explicit-topic-known process ARTICLES) + attribution (process=article topic, not vocab-guessed); same extractor/store/held-out/seed

diagnosis.headline: DENSE/EXPLICIT topic-known reading RECOVERS substantial process-conditioned knowledge per process where the article's entities match the held-out -- REFUTING the overstated 'reading can't supply the knowledge'. The AGGREGATE is capped by corpus VOLUME + specific mismatches, not by a fundamental reading limit.
diagnosis.why_aggregate_below_v4: LOW CORPUS VOLUME: 18 SimpleWiki articles = 1229 sentences -> only 155 facts, vs v4's ~735 facts from a far larger scattered scan. Fewer facts -> lower aggregate coverage even though per-fact quality/attribution is higher.

failure_localization.hydrocarbon_formation: reader extracted 32 facts but 0 held-out recall -> ENTITY MISMATCH (article about coal/oil surface entities; ProPara DEV hydrocarbon participants differ). Content/held-out mismatch, NOT reader depth.
failure_localization.fossilization: 0 facts extracted from the 63-sentence Fossil article -> the article is DESCRIPTIVE (what fossils are) not MECHANISTIC (X is consumed/produced) -> ARTICLE CONTENT limit, not reader depth.

diagnosis.corpus_was_the_confound: CONFIRMED for well-matched processes (electricity_generation 0.561, igneous_rock_cycle 0.692, combustion 0.452, erosion 0.60, digestion 0.50 -- approaching the seed, far above the scramble floor). The remaining limits are (a) VOLUME (need more dense articles per process -- full Wikipedia/OpenStax, not one SimpleWiki stub) and (b) per-process content/entity mismatch, NOT a fundamental 'reading can't learn' ceiling.
diagnosis.next_lever: more dense process-text per process (full-Wikipedia articles or OpenStax chapters) to raise volume; and process-held-out entity alignment for hydrocarbon_formation/fossilization.

final_verdict_msg: MIDDLE_BAND (overstated conclusion CORRECTED): dense/explicit topic-known process-ARTICLE reading RECOVERS substantial process-conditioned entity-fate knowledge per process -- electricity_generation 0.561/(seed 0.6585), igneous_rock_cycle 0.6923/(seed 0.8462), combustion 0.4516, erosion 0.60, digestion 0.50 -- APPROACHING the seed and FAR above the ~0.1879 scramble floor, which the scattered v4 baseline never achieved per-process. This REFUTES 'reading can't supply the knowledge'. HOWEVER the AGGREGATE reading_only=0.2121 is below v4-scattered 0.2788 because the dense corpus is SMALL (1229 sentences -> 155 facts vs v4 ~735) AND two processes fail for locatable reasons: hydrocarbon_formation 0.0 (entity mismatch, 32 facts extracted), fossilization 0 facts (descriptive not mechanistic article). CONCLUSION: the corpus WAS a confound -- dense explicit reading CAN learn process-conditioned physics; the residual limits are corpus VOLUME + per-process content/entity alignment, NOT a fundamental reading ceiling. Next lever: more dense process-text per process.
